page: Amazon Web Services i7i.4xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the Intel Xeon 8559C processor. Configured with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores at 3.2 GHz, the system features dedicated CPU allocation and hyper-threading on the x86_64 architecture. Memory provisions include 128 GB of high-frequency 6 GHz DDR5 RAM, equating to an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a direct-attached 3750 GB NVMe SSD volume, while network throughput provides a baseline bandwidth of 9 Gbps without integrated GPU hardware.

Performance profiles demonstrate significant single-threaded speed and memory transfer rates. The instance achieves a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2308.0 and top-tier text processing performance of 2840.0. Large-block uncached memory write throughput registers at 91.67 GB/s, reflecting the high throughput of DDR5 architecture alongside a PassMark memory score of 2799.27. Multithreaded workloads yield middle-tier results, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 13730.0 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 113.15 GB/s, bounded by its 16 vCPU allocation.

The bundled NVMe storage and large DDR5 capacity position this instance efficiently for I/O-intensive workloads, eliminating the network latency and separate billing constructs typical of attached block volumes. It is suited for transactional databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, real-time analytics engines, and cache systems like Redis, which recorded 24.61 million SET operations per second in testing.
description: Amazon Web Services i7i.4xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual machine operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with an Intel Xeon 8559C processor delivering 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores) at 3.2 GHz, 128 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, and 3750 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The instance features a 9 Gbps baseline network capacity and lacks discrete GPU acceleration. Benchmark testing highlights top-decile single-core metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 2308.0, alongside strong uncached memory write rates of 91.67 GB/s and rapid single-threaded compression performance. Multithreaded CPU benchmarks remain within average ranges relative to its 16-thread capacity. The high memory ratio and high-capacity local NVMe array make the i7i.4xlarge suitable for high-throughput databases, memory-backed indexing, in-memory caching platforms, and data warehousing tasks requiring low-latency storage access.
